audience.text: Python developers who need to parse, inspect, and extract content from OneNote notebooks programmatically, especially for document analysis, content migration, or PDF reporting workflows.

capabilities.text: Parse .one files from a path or binary stream into a DOM tree of Page, Outline, OutlineElement, RichText, Image, Table, and AttachedFile nodes.
capabilities.title: Parse OneNote .one files

capabilities.text: Traverse the document tree using CompositeNode.GetChildNodes() for type-based search or DocumentVisitor for full traversal.
capabilities.title: Traverse document structure

capabilities.text: Extract rich text with per-run formatting (bold, italic, underline, hyperlinks, font, color) via TextRun and TextStyle, and paragraph-level styling via ParagraphStyle.
capabilities.title: Extract rich text with formatting

capabilities.text: Export pages to PDF using Document.Save with SaveFormat.Pdf and PdfSaveOptions for configurable JPEG quality and image compression.
capabilities.title: Export pages to PDF

capabilities.text: Extract embedded images and attached files as raw bytes with FileName and dimensions for saving to disk.
capabilities.title: Extract images and attachments

capabilities.text: Inspect tables (Table, TableRow, TableCell), OneNote tags (NoteTag), and numbered lists (NumberList) with their properties.
capabilities.title: Inspect tables, tags, and lists

limitations.text: Writing back to .one files is not implemented — this library only reads OneNote files.
LoadOptions.DocumentPassword and encrypted documents are not supported — supplying a password raises IncorrectPasswordException.
SaveFormat currently declares only Pdf — Document.Save raises UnsupportedSaveFormatException for any other format or options object.
License.SetLicense() and Metered.SetMeteredKey() are no-ops in this edition — no license is required to use this library.
DetectLayoutChanges() is a compatibility stub and performs no layout computation.
FileFormat always reports OneNote2010 regardless of source file version.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic access to OneNote content (pages, rich text, images, tables, tags, attachments, numbered lists) without requiring Microsoft OneNote installation or COM automation.
Supports exporting OneNote pages to PDF with configurable image compression and JPEG quality for reporting and archival purposes.
Provides a DOM-based traversal API using DocumentVisitor and GetChildNodes to inspect document structure and extract specific node types.
Allows extraction of embedded images and attached files as raw bytes for further processing or archival.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Note FOSS for Python is a free, open-source Python library for reading Microsoft OneNote .one files and exporting pages to PDF, with no dependency on Microsoft OneNote or COM automation.

workflows.name: Load and inspect OneNote document
workflows.text: Load a .one file using Document, then inspect its display name and count pages using iteration and len.

workflows.name: Extract rich text with formatting
workflows.text: Traverse RichText nodes and access TextRuns to read text and per-run formatting including hyperlinks, bold, italic, and font properties.

workflows.name: Export to PDF with options
workflows.text: Call Document.Save with SaveFormat.Pdf and PdfSaveOptions to export pages to PDF with configurable JPEG quality and image compression.

workflows.name: Extract embedded images
workflows.text: Iterate over Image nodes, access FileName and Bytes, and write bytes to disk to save embedded images.

workflows.name: Inspect tables and tags
workflows.text: Traverse Table, TableRow, TableCell nodes to extract cell values, and inspect NoteTag objects attached to text, images, and tables.

workflows.name: Count document nodes
workflows.text: Subclass DocumentVisitor and override VisitPageStart, VisitRichTextStart, VisitImageStart to count pages, rich text, and images.
